doc.title: Virtual Machine
doc.para: TJS2 VM TJS2 compiles scripts into binary code for a virtual machine (TJS2 VM) before executing them. Since the disassembly result of this TJS2 VM code is displayed when an exception occurs or when a dump is performed, this virtual machine is briefly explained below.

Instruction Code The TJS2 VM is independent for each execution unit such as functions and properties, and no single function shares instruction code space, register space, flags, or constant area with other functions. The instruction pointer (ip) always starts at 0 at the beginning of a function or similar unit. Instruction codes represented by simple names that are easy for humans to read are called mnemonics.

Registers Registers in the TJS2 VM are represented in mnemonics as %(number). Numbers can also be negative. There is no limit on the number of registers. Local variables, temporary values during calculations, etc., are all recorded in registers. Main memory and stacks do not exist. The values represented by registers are the same as TJS2 variables, and can represent integers, real numbers, objects, strings, octet sequences, and void. In the current version, register %0 is always void. Register %-1 is this. Register %-2 is a special object called this proxy; when a member reference is made to this object, it first looks at this, and if not found there, looks at global. The this proxy does not exist in execution units at the global level. Arguments to functions and the like start execution pre-stored in registers such as %-3, %-4, etc. Values of registers other than those whose purpose is predetermined or whose values are set prior to execution are undefined at the start of execution.
Flags The TJS2 VM has only one flag, where comparison results are stored. The flag takes only true or false values.

Constant Area The constant area of the TJS2 VM is a location to store constants, represented as *(number) in mnemonics. The constant area is read-only, and the const instruction is used to move values from this constant area to registers. In addition, "names" used to access object members by name, such as function names and property names, are also stored in this constant area.

VM Mnemonic List Some operands take the format %obj.*name or %obj.%name; these involve member references to objects. Operands in the format %obj.*name perform direct reference, referencing the member named *name from the object represented by register %obj. Operands in the format %obj.%name perform indirect reference, referencing the member named %name from the object represented by register %obj. Mnemonics for such instructions have suffixes d or pd (direct / property direct), or i or pi (indirect / property indirect). Instructions with p in the suffix trigger the property handler of the target register (operating as the unary '*' operator).
nop(no operation)
Does nothing.
const(copy constant value)
Format: const %dest, *src Copies the value in the constant area indicated by *src to the register indicated by %dest.
cp(copy register)
Format: cp %dest, %src Copies the value of the register indicated by %src to the register indicated by %dest.
cl(clear register)
Format: cl %dest Sets the register indicated by %dest to void.
ccl(clear register)
Format: ccl %low-%high Sets all registers in the range from the register indicated by %low to the register indicated by %high to void.
tt(test true)
Format: tt %reg If the register indicated by %reg represents true, sets the flag to true; if it represents false, sets the flag to false.
tf(test false)
Format: tf %reg Opposite of tt; if the register indicated by %reg represents true, sets the flag to false; if it represents false, sets the flag to true.
ceq(compare equal)
Format: ceq %reg1, %reg2 If %reg1 and %reg2 match in normal comparison (behavior of the == operator), sets the flag to true; otherwise sets it to false.
cdeq(compare distinct equal)
Format: cdeq %reg1, %reg2 If %reg1 and %reg2 match in strict comparison (behavior of the === operator), sets the flag to true; otherwise sets it to false.
clt(compare littler than)
Format: clt %reg1, %reg2 If %reg1 > %reg2, sets the flag to true; otherwise sets it to false.
cgt(compare greater than)
Format: cgt %reg1, %reg2 If %reg1 < %reg2, sets the flag to true; otherwise sets it to false.
setf(set flag)
Format: setf %dest If the flag is true, sets %dest to true (non-zero integer); if false, sets it to false (integer 0).
setnf(set not flag)
Format: setnf %dest Opposite of setf; if the flag is false, sets %dest to true (non-zero integer); if true, sets it to false (integer 0).
lnot(logical not)
Format: lnot %reg Reverses the boolean value of %reg.
nf(not flag)
Format: nf Reverses the flag's boolean value.
jf(jump if flag)
Format: jf ip Jumps to ip if the flag is true.
jnf(jump if not flag)
Format: jnf ip Jumps to ip if the flag is false.
inc, incpd, incpi, incp(increment)
Format: inc %reg Format: incpd %res, %obj.*name Format: incpi %res, %obj.%name Format: incp %res, %propobj
Increments %reg, %obj.*name, %obj.%name, or %propobj. Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
dec, decpd, decpi, decp(decrement)
Format: dec %reg Format: decpd %res, %obj.*name Format: decpi %res, %obj.%name Format: decp %res, %propobj
Decrements %reg, %obj.*name, %obj.%name, or %propobj. Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
lor, lorpd, lorpi, lorp(logical or)
Format: lor %dest, %src Performs logical OR of %dest and %src, and stores the result in %dest. Format: lorpd %res, %obj.*name, %src Performs logical OR of %obj.*name and %src, and stores the result in %obj.*name. Format: lorpi %res, %obj.%name, %src Performs logical OR of %obj.%name and %src, and stores the result in %obj.%name. Format: lorp %res, %propobj, %src Performs logical OR of %propobj and %src, and stores the result in %propobj. Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
land, landpd, landpi, landp(logical and)
Format: land %dest, %src Performs logical AND of %dest and %src, and stores the result in %dest. Format: landpd %res, %obj.*name, %src Performs logical AND of %obj.*name and %src, and stores the result in %obj.*name. Format: landpi %res, %obj.%name, %src Performs logical AND of %obj.%name and %src, and stores the result in %obj.%name. Format: landp %res, %propobj, %src Performs logical AND of %propobj and %src, and stores the result in %propobj. Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
bor, borpd, borpi, borp(bitwise or)
Format: bor %dest, %src Performs bitwise OR of %dest and %src, and stores the result in %dest. Format: borpd %res, %obj.*name, %src Performs bitwise OR of %obj.*name and %src, and stores the result in %obj.*name. Format: borpi %res, %obj.%name, %src Performs bitwise OR of %obj.%name and %src, and stores the result in %obj.%name. Format: borp %res, %propobj, %src Performs bitwise OR of %propobj and %src, and stores the result in %propobj. Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
bxor, bxorpd, bxorpi, bxorp(bitwise xor)
Format: bxor %dest, %src Performs bitwise XOR of %dest and %src, and stores the result in %dest. Format: bxorpd %res, %obj.*name, %src Performs bitwise XOR of %obj.*name and %src, and stores the result in %obj.*name. Format: bxorpi %res, %obj.%name, %src Performs bitwise XOR of %obj.%name and %src, and stores the result in %obj.%name. Format: bxorp %res, %propobj, %src Performs bitwise XOR of %propobj and %src, and stores the result in %propobj. Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
band, bandpd, bandpi, bandp(bitwise and)
Format: band %dest, %src Performs bitwise AND of %dest and %src, and stores the result in %dest. Format: bandpd %res, %obj.*name, %src Performs bitwise AND of %obj.*name and %src, and stores the result in %obj.*name. Format: bandpi %res, %obj.%name, %src Performs bitwise AND of %obj.%name and %src, and stores the result in %obj.%name. Format: bandp %res, %propobj, %src Performs bitwise AND of %propobj and %src, and stores the result in %propobj. Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
sar, sarpd, sarpi, sarp(shift arithmetic right)
Format: sar %dest, %src Performs arithmetic right shift on %dest by the count represented by %src, and stores the result in %dest. Format: sarpd %res, %obj.*name, %src Performs arithmetic right shift on %obj.*name by the count represented by %src, and stores the result in %obj.*name. Format: sarpi %res, %obj.%name, %src Performs arithmetic right shift on %obj.%name by the count represented by %src, and stores the result in %obj.%name. Format: sarp %res, %propobj, %src Performs arithmetic right shift on %propobj by the count represented by %src, and stores the result in %propobj. Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
sal, salpd, salpi, salp(shift arithmetic left)
Format: sal %dest, %src Performs arithmetic left shift on %dest by the count represented by %src, and stores the result in %dest. Format: salpd %res, %obj.*name, %src Performs arithmetic left shift on %obj.*name by the count represented by %src, and stores the result in %obj.*name. Format: salpi %res, %obj.%name, %src Performs arithmetic left shift on %obj.%name by the count represented by %src, and stores the result in %obj.%name. Format: salp %res, %propobj, %src Performs arithmetic left shift on %propobj by the count represented by %src, and stores the result in %propobj. Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
sr, srpd, srpi, srp(shift bitwise right)
Format: sr %dest, %src Performs bitwise right shift on %dest by the count represented by %src, and stores the result in %dest. Format: srpd %res, %obj.*name, %src Performs bitwise right shift on %obj.*name by the count represented by %src, and stores the result in %obj.*name. Format: srpi %res, %obj.%name, %src Performs bitwise right shift on %obj.%name by the count represented by %src, and stores the result in %obj.%name. Format: srp %res, %propobj, %src Performs bitwise right shift on %propobj by the count represented by %src, and stores the result in %propobj. Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
add, addpd, addpi, addp(add)
Format: add %dest, %src Adds %src to %dest, and stores the result in %dest. Format: addpd %res, %obj.*name, %src Adds %src to %obj.*name, and stores the result in %obj.*name. Format: addpi %res, %obj.%name, %src Adds %src to %obj.%name, and stores the result in %obj.%name. Format: addp %res, %propobj, %src Adds %src to %propobj, and stores the result in %propobj. Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
sub, subpd, subpi, subp(subtract)
Format: sub %dest, %src Subtracts %src from %dest, and stores the result in %dest. Format: subpd %res, %obj.*name, %src Subtracts %src from %obj.*name, and stores the result in %obj.*name. Format: subpi %res, %obj.%name, %src Subtracts %src from %obj.%name, and stores the result in %obj.%name. Format: subp %res, %propobj, %src Subtracts %src from %propobj, and stores the result in %propobj. Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
mod, modpd, modpi, modp(modulo)
Format: mod %dest, %src Stores the remainder of %dest divided by %src into %dest. Format: modpd %res, %obj.*name, %src Stores the remainder of %obj.*name divided by %src into %obj.*name. Format: modpi %res, %obj.%name, %src Stores the remainder of %obj.%name divided by %src into %obj.%name. Format: modp %res, %propobj, %src Stores the remainder of %propobj divided by %src into %propobj. Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
div, divpd, divpi, divp(real divide)
Format: div %dest, %src Performs real division of %dest by %src, and stores the result in %dest. Format: divpd %res, %obj.*name, %src Performs real division of %obj.*name by %src, and stores the result in %obj.*name. Format: divpi %res, %obj.%name, %src Performs real division of %obj.%name by %src, and stores the result in %obj.%name. Format: divp %res, %propobj, %src Performs real division of %propobj by %src, and stores the result in %propobj. Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
idiv, idivpd, idivpi, idivp(integer divide)
Format: idiv %dest, %src Performs integer division of %dest by %src, and stores the result in %dest. Format: idivpd %res, %obj.*name, %src Performs integer division of %obj.*name by %src, and stores the result in %obj.*name. Format: idivpi %res, %obj.%name, %src Performs integer division of %obj.%name by %src, and stores the result in %obj.%name. Format: divp %res, %propobj, %src Performs integer division of %propobj by %src, and stores the result in %propobj. Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
mul, mulpd, mulpi, mulp(multiply)
Format: mul %dest, %src Multiplies %dest by %src, and stores the result in %dest. Format: mulpd %res, %obj.*name, %src Multiplies %obj.*name by %src, and stores the result in %obj.*name. Format: mulpi %res, %obj.%name, %src Multiplies %obj.%name by %src, and stores the result in %obj.%name. Format: mulp %res, %propobj, %src Multiplies %propobj by %src, and stores the result in %propobj. Among the above instructions, for those having %res as a parameter, if res is not 0, the result is also stored in %res.
bnot(bitwise not)
Format: bnot %reg Reverses the bits of %reg and stores it back in %reg.
asc(make ascii string)
Format: asc %reg Creates a single character corresponding to the numeric value represented by %reg, and stores it back in %reg.
chr(cheracter code)
Format: chr %reg Stores the character code of the first character of the string represented by %reg into %reg.
num(number)
Format: num %reg Converts the register represented by %reg to a number.
chs(change sign)
Format: chs %reg Reverses the sign of the numeric value of the register represented by %reg.
inv(invalidate)
Format: inv %reg Invalidates the object represented by %reg.
chkinv(invalidate)
Format: chkinv %reg If the object represented by %reg is not invalidated, sets %reg to true; otherwise sets it to false.
int(convert to integer)
Format: int %reg Converts the register represented by %reg to an integer.
real(convert to real)
Format: real %reg Converts the register represented by %reg to a real number.
string(convert to string)
Format: string %reg Converts the register represented by %reg to a string.
octet(convert to octet)
Format: octet %reg Converts the register represented by %reg to an octet sequence.
typeof, typeofd, typeofi(check type)
Format: typeof %reg Format: typeofd %obj.*name Format: typeofi %obj.%name
Checks the type of %reg, %obj.*name, or %obj.%name, and stores a string representing that type back into %reg, %obj.*name, or %obj.%name.
eval(evaluate expression)
Format: eval %reg Executes the string represented by %reg as an expression and stores the result back in %reg.
eexp(execute expression)
Format: eexp %reg Executes the string represented by %reg as an expression and discards the result.
chkins(check instance)
Format: chkins %reg, %classname If the object represented by %reg is an instance of the class named %classname, stores true in %reg; otherwise stores false.
call, calld, calli(function call)
Format: call %dest, %func(%arg1, %arg2, %arg3, ...) Format: calld %dest, %obj.*name(%arg1, %arg2, %arg3, ...) Format: calli %dest, %obj.%name(%arg1, %arg2, %arg3, ...)
Calls the function object represented by %func, %obj.*name, or %obj.%name with arguments %arg1, %arg2, %arg3 ..., and stores the result in %dest. If %dest is %0, the result is discarded (without being stored in %0).
new(create new)
Format: new %dest, %func(%arg1, %arg2, %arg3, ...) Constructs the class object represented by %func with arguments %arg1, %arg2, %arg3 ..., and stores the result in %dest.
gpd, gpds(get property direct)
Format: gpd %dest, %obj.*name Format: gpds %dest, %obj.*name
References the member represented by *name from the object represented by %obj and copies its value to %dest. gpd involves invoking a property handler, but gpds does not invoke a property handler and gets the property object itself.
gpi, gpis(get property indirect)
Format: gpi %dest, %obj.%name Format: gpis %dest, %obj.%name
References the member represented by %name from the object represented by %obj and copies its value to %dest. gpi involves invoking a property handler, but gpis does not invoke a property handler and gets the property object itself.
spd, spde, spdeh, spds(set property direct)
Format: spd %obj.*name Format: spde %obj.*name Format: spdeh %obj.*name Format: spds %obj.*name
Assigns the value of %src to the member represented by *name of the object represented by %obj. spd performs normal access, but throws an exception if the member does not exist. spde creates a new member if the member does not exist. spdeh sets the member as a hidden member. It has no meaning in the current version. spds does not invoke a property handler and replaces the property object itself.
spi, spie, spis(set property indirect)
Format: spi %obj.%name Format: spie %obj.%name Format: spis %obj.%name
Assigns the value of %src to the member represented by %name of the object represented by %obj. spi performs normal access, but throws an exception if the member does not exist. spie creates a new member if the member does not exist. spis does not invoke a property handler and replaces the property object itself.
getp
Format: getp %reg, %propobj
Triggers the getter of the property object represented by %propobj, obtains the value of the property, and assigns it to %reg. Operates as the unary '*' operator.
setp
Format: setp %propobj, %reg
Triggers the setter of the property object represented by %propobj and sets the value of %reg. Operates as the unary '*' operator.
deld, deli(delete member)
Format: deld %reg, %obj.*name Format: deli %reg, %obj.%name
Deletes the member represented by *name or %name of the object represented by %obj. Stores a boolean indicating whether the deletion succeeded into %reg, but if %reg is %0, the result is discarded.
srv(set result value)
Format: srv %reg Sets the value of %reg as the function return value (the return value of the function becomes the value represented by %reg).
ret(return)
Format: ret Returns to the caller.
entry(enter try block)
Format: entry ip, %reg Enters an exception-protected block. If an exception occurs, jumps to ip and sets the exception object in %reg.
extry(exit from try block)
Format: extry Exits from the exception-protected block.
throw(throw exception object)
Format: throw %reg Throws the object represented by %reg as an exception object.
chgthis(change this)
Format: chgthis %dest, %src Changes the closure part of the object represented by %dest to the object indicated by %src.
global(get global object)
Format: global %dest Stores the global object in %dest.
addci(add class instance information)
Format: addci %dest, %info Adds %info to the class instance information of the object represented by %dest.
regmember(register members)
Format: regmember Registers class members into the "this" object. Used internally.
debugger(call debugger)
Format: debugger Suspends execution and calls the debugger. In the current version implementation, it calls a native debugger instead of the TJS2 debugger.
